newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Arafat sees Moroccan king over U.S. summit.
newsitem.headline: Arafat sees Moroccan king over U.S. summit.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat on Thursday briefed Morocco's King Hassan on the Middle East summit in Washington, which was termed a failure by advisers to Arafat's Palestinian Authority.
Arafat arrived at the palace at Skhirat at 1.15 p.m (13.15 GMT) in bright shinesun. The Palestinian president inspected a white-uniformed royal guard of honor and then was greeted by King Hassan.
The two leaders shook hands warmly and embraced. Arafat was also welcomed by Prime Minister Adellatif Filali.

Arafat, accompagnied by adviser Mahmoud Abbas better known as Abu Mazen, then went with the king for a closed-door meeting. Arafat said earlier he had came to Morocco to brief the king on the Middle East summit.
"I can make no comment until I have seen King Hassan," said Arafat at Rabat airport. He was expected to leave later for Paris.

Arafat arrived aboard a Saudi airliner from the summit with Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, Jordan's King Hussein and U.S. President Bill Clinton. It ended on Wednesday with few results other than agreement to resume low-level Israeli-Palestinian talks.
"There were no positive results due to the Israeli position of refusing to deal seriously with basic issues," said Yasser Abed Rabbo, an adviser to the Palestinian Authority.
